subject: physics
question:
QUESTION
Explain distance, displacement, speed and velocity for JEE from the basics. Cover: frame of reference, origin and positive direction, why motion is relative; distance as path length versus displacement with a sign; average speed as total distance over time versus average velocity as displacement over time; instantaneous velocity dx/dt, speed as its magnitude. Draw one simple diagram: a straight track with A at x = 0, B at x = 40 m, C at x = 10 m, the car going A to B then back to C.

Independently solve every requested unknown and return one complete checked plan.

qualitativeClaims.claim: A frame of reference specifies an observer, an origin and a positive coordinate direction. Position and motion are measured relative to that frame; observers in different frames can assign different velocities to the same car.
qualitativeClaims.expected: Take A as the origin and increasing x, toward B, as positive.

qualitativeClaims.claim: The straight-track diagram must locate the points by coordinate and show the car travelling from A to B, then reversing to C.
qualitativeClaims.expected: Along increasing x: A (0 m), C (10 m), B (40 m); journey A → B → C.

qualitativeClaims.claim: Distance adds the lengths of every part of the path; it is a nonnegative scalar, even when the car reverses.
qualitativeClaims.expected: For this journey, total distance is 70 m.

qualitativeClaims.claim: Displacement is final position minus initial position. Its sign specifies direction on the chosen axis; the return leg has negative displacement, while the whole journey ends in the positive direction.
For any positive elapsed time Δt for the entire journey, average speed uses total path length, whereas average velocity uses signed displacement.
qualitativeClaims.expected: average speed = 70 m/Δt; average velocity = +10 m/Δt. No numerical rates follow without Δt.

qualitativeClaims.claim: Instantaneous velocity is the signed rate of change of position; instantaneous speed is its nonnegative magnitude.
qualitativeClaims.expected: v=dx/dt; speed=|v|. On the return leg, velocity is negative wherever the car is moving.

lawIds: one-dimensional distance as sum of absolute position changes
displacement as final position minus initial position
average speed as total distance divided by elapsed time
average velocity as displacement divided by elapsed time
assumptions: Use the stated straight track as the one-dimensional path and take increasing x as positive.
No travel time or position-versus-time function is supplied.
